official.deadline_central_display: 18 September 2026 at 12:00 (Belgian time, UTC+1) - the 2027-2028 call, now closed; the next call is announced for August 2027
official.deadline_note: The call opened on 3 August 2026 and closed on 18 September 2026 at 12:00 Belgian time. ARES states the next call will open in August 2027. There is no rolling deadline.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 call of the five-year international academic cooperation programme 2027-2032, funded by the Belgian Directorate General for Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid; opened 3 August 2026, closed 18 September 2026
official.status_note: ARES states that the 2027-2028 call is closed and that the next call opens in August 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship includes tuition fees (frais d'inscription) for the specialised bachelor's degree and the specialised master's degrees only; the continuing-education certificate covers indirect mission expenses instead.
benefits: International travel expenses: economy class on an IATA airline, maximum one return trip per academic year
Subsistence allowance as a monthly package for 12 months (plus a reduced 13th month) for the specialised bachelor's and specialised master's degrees
Tuition fees for the specialised bachelor's and specialised master's degrees
Exceptional costs related to visa applications up to EUR 200, included in the subsistence allowance; the excess is reimbursed on actual costs against supporting documents
Travel between establishments up to EUR 250, reimbursed on justified actual costs
Insurance costs paid directly by ARES
For continuing education: a monthly allowance for the duration of the course, a fixed EUR 200 for additional international travel costs and indirect mission expenses
100 scholarships were available for the 2027-2028 academic year
eligibility: Be a permanent resident of and work in one of the 32 eligible ARES partner countries; people of Palestinian nationality are eligible even if they do not reside in one of these countries
Hold a higher education diploma and meet the admission conditions of the training, as described on the ARES website
The relevant academic degree must have been obtained no more than 20 years before the start of the training, a limit extended by one year per childbirth and/or adoption
Show at least two years of relevant professional occupation in one of the 32 eligible countries, after the last higher education diploma and before the closing date of the call
requirements: Apply through the GIRAF platform with a validated GIRAF account; account creation is requested through ARES if you do not have one
Meet the admission conditions of the specific programme applied for
Submit a complete file: once the application is submitted it can no longer be modified
Applying is free of charge; ARES charges no fee at any stage of the application or selection process
documents: GIRAF account (created and validated by ARES) giving access to the application form under 'Competitive Calls'
Completed application form submitted through GIRAF ('Candidature - Formation internationale 2027-2028'), which cannot be modified after submission
Reference document of the call and applicant's guide, downloadable from the ARES call page
selection_criteria: Selection is run per programme by a jury
Applications are screened for admissibility against the residency, diploma, diploma age and professional experience criteria before evaluation
Appeals against the selection decision may be lodged with the Belgian Council of State
coverage: International travel expenses (economy class, one return trip per academic year)
Subsistence allowance (monthly package for 12 months plus a reduced 13th month for degree programmes)
Tuition fees for the specialised bachelor's and specialised master's degrees
Insurance costs, paid directly by ARES
Visa-related exceptional costs up to EUR 200 and inter-establishment travel up to EUR 250 on justified actual costs
application_method: Have or request a GIRAF account validated by ARES
Log in to GIRAF, go to 'Competitive Calls' and click the 'Application - International Training 2027-2028' button once
Complete and save the form fields, then click 'Submit my application'; the file then appears under 'My Submitted Applications' and can no longer be modified
Use the applicant's guide published by ARES for help
official.application_route: Create or reuse a validated GIRAF account, open the 'International Training' application under Competitive Calls, complete the form and submit it before the 12:00 Belgian-time deadline; the file is locked once submitted.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be permanent residents of and work in one of the 32 ARES partner countries; people of Palestinian nationality are eligible without that residency condition. Award holders are expected to return to their country of origin or another country and apply the training acquired in Belgium to development purposes, for example through a work contract or a formal commitment, producing a multiplier effect.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship exists precisely to bring candidates from ARES partner countries to study in Belgium
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Training must address development-related issues and be one of the programmes offered in the call: for 2027-2028 one specialised bachelor's degree (Digital Integrated Supply Chain), eight specialised master's degrees and one continuing-education certificate (operations in cybersecurity and risk governance)
official.duration: Specialised bachelor's and specialised master's degrees: 12 months maximum (one academic year). Continuing training: 6 months maximum.
official.description: ARES, the Wallonia-Brussels Federation academy for research and higher education, awards international training scholarships so that professionals residing and working in its partner countries can follow a specialised bachelor's degree, a specialised master's degree or a short continuing-education course in a FWB institution in Belgium, within a five-year programme financed by Belgian development cooperation.
official.program_type: Government scholarship of the Wallonia-Brussels government, administered by ARES

applicant_utility.summary: The decisive filter here is not academic but professional: ARES wants someone who already holds a relevant higher education diploma no older than 20 years and has at least two years of relevant work in one of the 32 partner countries, so recent graduates with no work history are excluded before anyone reads a transcript. Applications run through GIRAF, the form opens only once, and once you press submit the file is frozen, so assemble everything - including evidence of your professional experience - before you start typing. Only ten programmes were on offer for 2027-2028, so the choice of programme is effectively the choice of scholarship.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career professionals from an ARES partner country who already hold a relevant diploma and want a one-year specialised degree in Belgium with a development focus.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country is one of the 32 partner countries and that you hold permanent residency and work there
Count the years since your diploma: it must be no more than 20 years at the start of the training, with one extra year per childbirth or adoption
Document at least two years of relevant professional experience in an eligible country, after your last diploma and before the call closes
Request or check your GIRAF account early, since ARES must validate it before you can open the form
Download the reference document of the call and the applicant's guide, and read the admission conditions of the specific programme before committing
common_rejection_risks: Applying straight after graduation: the two-year professional experience requirement is the most discriminating condition
A diploma older than the 20-year limit with no childbirth or adoption adjustment
Residence or work outside the 32 eligible countries (the only exception is Palestinian nationality)
Submitting an incomplete or imperfect file, since the application cannot be modified after submission
Choosing a programme whose own admission conditions you do not meet
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: ARES does not publish the amount of the subsistence allowance, so the personal share is unknown in advance; only travel, insurance, tuition (for degree tracks) and small capped extras are covered, and the visa allowance is capped at EUR 200 inside the subsistence allowance.
document_audit: Visa costs above EUR 200 are reimbursed only on actual costs with supporting documents, so keep every receipt
Inter-establishment travel is capped at EUR 250 and must be justified with actual-cost evidence
Professional experience must be evidenced for a period after the last diploma, not merely claimed in the form
The application form can be opened only once - do not click the button to explore it
alerts: The 2027-2028 call closed on 18 September 2026; the next one opens in August 2027, so a missed window costs a full year
Applying is free: ARES warns that anyone asking for payment by email while claiming to act for ARES should be reported to scholarships-cooperation@ares-ac.be
Award holders commit to returning to their country or another country and using the training for development purposes, with a multiplier effect
Appeals against the selection decision can be lodged with the Belgian Council of State
The continuing-education track works differently: no tuition coverage, a monthly allowance for the course duration and a fixed EUR 200 travel costs allowance instead
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: GIRAF account validated by ARES, then one submission of the International Training application form during the August-September window; selection follows per programme.
